CBC/Radio-Canada’s parliamentary appropriation is a multi-hundred-million to billion-class annual public funding instrument. Private news bailout / subsidy programs (Local Journalism Initiative and related packages) are multi-hundred-million over multi-year windows. Ownership concentration among a small set of groups is documented in CRTC and industry data. “Captured board” language is inference…
On the record: appropriations, subsidy programs, ownership maps, CRTC decisions.

Inference (labeled): when the state funds both the public broadcaster and struggling private newsrooms, editorial independence is a structural accountability question. That is not proof of day-to-day editorial control without primary evidence of instruction.

Bell Media operates CTV — Canada's largest private television network — along with approximately 30 radio stations and multiple specialty channels (BNN Bloomberg, CP24, CTV News Channel, Discovery, Comedy, Much). Bell's parent BCE Inc. also owns Canada's largest telecommunications company. The same corporation that provides internet access and controls significant network infrastructure also…

Rogers Media operates Citytv (in Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg, Montreal), Sportsnet, and multiple radio and digital platforms. Rogers Communications, the parent company, is Canada's largest wireless carrier. Like Bell, the convergence of telecommunications infrastructure and media ownership means the same corporation that controls network access also controls significant news…

Postmedia Network owns the National Post, the Ottawa Citizen, the Calgary Herald, the Vancouver Sun, the Edmonton Journal, the Montreal Gazette, the Winnipeg Free Press (partial), and dozens of other daily and community newspapers.
